A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PALSGD. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including the algorithms, proofs, tables and figures, and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet-1K, TinyStories and CIFAR-10 experiments, including training times, accuracy, losses and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds worker-count simulations, multi-node experiments and further convergence analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same probabilistic local-gradient and pseudo-synchronization steps, periodic aggregation, decoupled optimizers and DDP warmup. Section 5 expands the proximal-regularization and moving-average explanations; its corrected update index does not establish a different procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix F extends evaluation from single-node systems to a multi-node communication environment using CIFAR-10/VGG-16 across up to eight nodes. The demonstrated datasets and prediction tasks remain CIFAR-10, ImageNet-1K and TinyStories. V1's unelaborated WikiText/QNLI statements disappear, but neither PDF provides corresponding results establishing that experiments were removed.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 1 adds an explicit Local SGD comparison alongside DDP, DiLoCo and PALSGD in the small-CNN worker-count experiment. V1 mentions Local SGD but does not report this comparison. The retained large-model comparisons still use DDP and DiLoCo; newly discussed asynchronous methods and SCAFFOLD are not evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 adds 100-epoch small-CNN simulations with 4–64 workers and multi-node VGG-16 evaluations with 4–32 GPUs, batch size 256 per GPU, no learning-rate decay and adjusted warmups. Appendices D and E.3 introduce step-to-target and optimizer time-to-target comparisons. Appendix B also changes GPT-Neo-8M's stated H from 16 to 64, although retained captions still specify 16; this does not establish rerunning.

E4.justification: V2 adds worker-scaling analyses, global-step comparisons that distinguish optimization progress from communication savings, and an outer-optimizer time-to-target ablation. These substantially extend the questions examined. The original seed, optimizer-loss, eta, p and H analyses remain, with Appendix D's ablations moved to Appendix E.

E5.justification: The three seeds, 2022, 2023 and 2024, and their mean/variance reporting are unchanged, including all values in v1 Table 1 and v2 Table E.1. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or statistical testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Existing wall-clock results are retained, while substantial new results appear. Figure 1 reports 64-worker accuracies of 0.567 for PALSGD, 0.562 for DiLoCo, 0.519 for DDP and 0.192 for Local SGD. Figure D.3 newly reports 11,752 versus 13,973 validation-target steps for PALSGD and DDP on GPT-Neo-125M. Optimizer timing and multi-node runtime/accuracy results are also added; these are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: Theorems 1 and 2 replace the residual term (kappa + H/p) sigma^2/(mu T^2) with kappa H^2 sigma^2/(mu T^2). Appendix A.4 replaces the final step-size argument with differentiation and constrained minimization of g(alpha), removing the previous final restriction p <= 1/(kappa H). Assumptions and supporting lemmas largely remain. The new derivation contains reversed bounds implying 1/sqrt(A) <= 1/A^2 for A >= 4.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims about probabilistic pseudo-synchronization, communication efficiency, convergence and empirical effectiveness. The headline speedups of 18.4%, 24.4% and 21.1% are unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix D attributes ImageNet and GPT-Neo-8M wall-clock gains mainly to communication savings, while attributing GPT-Neo-125M gains to both communication savings and fewer optimization steps. Appendix F discusses accuracy degradation under large global batches, Appendix B limits simulation-based timing comparisons, and Section 8 newly acknowledges excluded asynchronous baselines. These materially refine the interpretation and applicability of the evidence.

D1.justification: V2 adds the small-CNN architecture in Table B.1, simulation hyperparameters, multi-node configuration and tuning details, and explicit memory/communication requirements. Appendix B replaces the anonymous code-access link with a named GitHub repository link. Most existing hardware, software and training documentation is retained; external resource availability was not verified.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion and citations for Parallel Restarted SGD, SCAFFOLD, DropCompute, Shadowheart SGD, SWIFT, model fragmentation and Omnivore. It sharpens distinctions concerning control variates, optimizer compatibility and fully asynchronous approaches while retaining the existing Local SGD/DiLoCo positioning.

P1.justification: Changes include targeted rewriting and retitling of Section 5, reorganized workload descriptions, an appendix contents page, and new analysis subsections. Existing ablations move from Appendix D to E. Publication headers, affiliations and acknowledgments are updated, while the overall narrative sequence and much of the original prose remain.

P2.justification: V2 adds six figures: the worker-count comparison, three global-step convergence figures, optimizer timing bars and multi-node scaling plots. It also adds the CNN architecture table. Existing plots are retained but renumbered, resized or repositioned, producing a substantial expansion of the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: The new multi-node experiments and global-step analyses make the efficiency claims better supported and clarify the source of gains beyond v1's wall-clock comparisons. Added implementation details and explicit comparison limitations also help assessment. These benefits support a limited net improvement, tempered by the erroneous new inequality in Appendix A.4 and the unresolved GPT-Neo-8M synchronization-interval inconsistency between Appendix B and retained captions.
